newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico overnight Cetes rate closes down sharply.
newsitem.headline: Mexico overnight Cetes rate closes down sharply.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down 95 basis points at 23.80 percent after a spectacular turnaround from earlier highs of 28.30 percent.
Traders said the reversal was due to speculation by major banks.

"There were two big banks which took advantage of the difficult situation we are in to speculate," said a trader. "What they did was hold on to their paper and sell it at low rates to brokerages that had no option, as they do not operate banks and have no access to the after-hours market."
Term instruments, however, gained on lack of demand and an unstable peso.
Rates on 90-day and 182-day Cetes rose by 150 and 30 basis points, respectively, to 29 and 29.30 percent.
Traders said the money market market was closely linked to the fortunes of the ailing peso during the session.

"When the peso began to recover, dealers began to calm down a little," one trader said. "Local and foreign investors began to buy paper, but speculation weighed far more heavily. We never thought the (overnight rate) would close where it did."

The benchmark 48-hour peso was 11.6 centavos weaker at 7.8250/7.8450 per dollar after an early bout of panic and speculation, but staggered back to close at 7.7800/7.7850 after foreign investors stepped into the stock market.
Total credit maturities for Thursday were estimated at about 3.2 billion pesos.
Traders saw overnight paper adjusting to levels of 26.50 percent on Thursday, which they said was more representative of Wednesday's trade.
